ROW.COLUMN: (ML/EN) Patterns of Recurring Originators/Beneficiaries in Funds Transfers

One of the major issues in money laundering surveillance is knowing your customers' customers. This is problematic in certain areas, such as correspondent banking, due to the incidence of nested bank relationships. Relationships may exist between entities external to the institution that utilize the institution or its correspondents as an intermediary for funds transfer activity. These hidden relationships may present vulnerabilities to money laundering, as the external entities can, without detection, wire funds between seemingly unrelated accounts at various institutions. Mantas monitors funds transfer activity and detects patterns of recurring transfers between originators and beneficiaries external to the institution. This enables more intelligent monitoring of funds associated with money laundering moving through the institution.

The scenario monitors activities between a pair of external entities for wire transaction. It grouped data on the dataset level and calculate parameters for the following pairs: Originator ? Beneficiary, Originator - Secondary Beneficiary, Secondary Originator ? Beneficiary, Secondary Originator - Secondary Beneficiary.
The dataset of the Primary Rule based on auxiliary datasets.
All scenario conditions are checked on dataset level. Highlights and scoring bindings are calculated in the primary rule. The sub-rule is used to restrict the transaction records in the alert analysis.
Because of different opposite party role the focal entities there is more then one match can be generated for the given focal entity.
